A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM-MapRepair work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original MANGO graph-construction and repair experiments, component ablations and model comparisons in Tables 1–2 and Appendix Tables A1–A4.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic, TextWorld, MANGO and literary-text experiments, plus algorithmic simulations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The core repair pipeline, normalized Edge Impact Score and Version Control operations remain. Appendix A adds a natural-text adaptation using angle and distance discretization with conflict-dependent elastic tolerances. The expanded history-based LCA description is presented as clarification, not evidence of a wholly new repair algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates MANGO interactive-fiction mapping. v2 retains that coverage and adds controlled synthetic error scenarios, procedurally generated TextWorld environments and mapping from Chapters 16–17 of Dream of the Red Chamber, substantially extending input conditions and domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds heuristic_remove and heuristic_modify as evaluated non-LLM comparators in the MANGO comparison. It also omits the VC-only comparator from that experiment, although VC-only remains in the synthetic ablation. These changes materially revise v1's comparison against unscaffolded and component-only LLM repair.

E3.justification: The stated repair budget changes from 10 attempts per conflict to 20 outer iterations and 3 attempts per conflict. v2 changes repair backbones, evaluates 42 GPT-4.1-built MANGO graphs containing 534 conflicts, and introduces controlled error-injection protocols. Evaluation expands from loops, conflict repair rate and repair accuracy to graph-level conflict-free rates, residual conflicts, structural preservation and natural-text recall.

E4.justification: v2 adds error-type and density ablations, an iteration-budget sensitivity sweep, six controlled algorithmic scenarios, a 1,160-graph LCA analysis and a structure-preservation analysis. The earlier advent walkthrough/repaired-map example and conflict-distribution visualization are removed.

E5.justification: v1 provides no seed counts or uncertainty intervals. v2 reports 20 independent seeds per synthetic cell, 30 game-seeds per TextWorld cell and 95% Wilson confidence intervals in Table 1. Appendix B adds variability reporting, while the cross-vendor discussion explicitly states that statistical significance was not formally assessed.

E6.justification: The original aggregate and per-game results are replaced by substantially different result sets. New findings include VC+EI achieving 25% conflict-free repair versus 70% for the baseline with eight directional errors (Table 1), and heuristic_remove leaving 98 conflicts versus 396 for the best LLM configuration (Table 3). Table 4 adds literary node/edge recall of 94.3%/88.2%. These are new evaluations, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces the earlier spatial-path LCA expression with a timestamp argmax over reasoning-history paths, formally introduces the commit-dependency domain and explains the local directional-conflict special case. v2 also removes the formal Conflict Revelation Gain definition and the assertion that PageRank convergence justifies equal feature weights, substantially revising the mathematical grounding.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain history-aware repair, Edge Impact scoring and MANGO refinement. v2 softens the dataset claim from eliminating structural conflicts to removing many inconsistencies, and foregrounds a natural-text recall benefit with explicit over-generation caveats instead of v1's broadly stated correctness and robustness benefit.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the simple component-synergy narrative with model-dependent recommendations and explanations of high-density failures. It adds substantial discussion of conflict reduction versus structural preservation, literary recall versus over-generation, limited single-novel validation and absent theoretical guarantees. The five-edge scoring correlation is explicitly qualified as a sanity check.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-experimental-data repository pointer, graph-generation and error-injection instructions, paragraph-level literary processing, expert ground-truth annotation details and the model-access proxy. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although precise discretization and elastic-optimization settings remain unspecified. The original six cleanup operations and edge-removal totals are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the TextWorld citation and removes several supporting references, including Jericho, g2o, bundle adjustment and some incremental scene-graph studies. The central positioning around SLAM-inspired consistency maintenance, knowledge-graph error management and LLM spatial reasoning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten, retained related-work and method explanations are condensed, and LCA exposition is expanded. Conclusion and Limitations become separate sections, while the long walkthrough appendix is replaced by a structured algorithmic-validation appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and replaces the conceptual Figure 1 with literary mapping comparisons and a rendered-map illustration. Figures 2–3 are retained, while the standalone version-history diagram and old appendix figures disappear. The aggregate and per-game table layouts are replaced with new experimental and algorithmic-analysis tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through controlled ablations with confidence intervals, independent algorithmic tests and non-LLM comparisons (Tables 1–3 and Appendix B). It also exposes failures and quantifies structural loss and over-generation, making the claims better calibrated than v1's broad reliability narrative. Removing per-game tables reduces audit detail, and the prose adaptation remains underspecified, but the gains in experimental rigor and interpretation outweigh these drawbacks.
